query: What are the top creative trends in Social Sciences related to evaluating job–housing balance impacts on migrant-worker burnout using longitudinal methods, spatial data, and ethical fieldwork?

response.query: What are the top creative trends in Social Sciences related to evaluating job–housing balance impacts on migrant-worker burnout using longitudinal methods, spatial data, and ethical fieldwork?
response.answer: Top trends include longitudinal studies, spatial data analysis, and ethical fieldwork to evaluate job-housing balance impacts on migrant-worker burnout. Researchers use mixed methods and spatial analytics for comprehensive insights. Ethical considerations are prioritized in fieldwork.

results.title: Granted projects | NWO
results.content: The proposed project aims to develop a new creative method - Affect Houses - to investigate the role of emotions in the encounters between burned-out teachers and their occupational physician. Moving beyond language, the proposed project explores the possibilities of an embodied approach to research in order to 1) give participants tools to express the full complexity and depth of their experiences regarding sick leave and return-to-work; 2) create opportunities for empathic understanding of these experiences; and 3) offer suggestions for improving return-to-work practices in education. This project will develop PoliBiasEU, a scalable, multilingual benchmark of political motions and votes from European parliaments, and conduct experiments to assess biases in LLMs. We will analyze ideological and entity biases, examine how persona prompts affect bias expression, and evaluate downstream impacts on political summarization and Q&A. Bringing together political theory on rights-claiming with international human rights law (IHRL) in an empirical legal study, this project maps the role irregular migrants play in developing IHRL through their formal and informal IHRL claims.
